name: Casablanca
tagline: Morocco's biggest city and its economic engine, home to one of the largest mosques in the world, an Art Deco downtown and a modern, cosmopolitan pulse.
highlight: The Hassan II Mosque at the edge of the Atlantic, its minaret rising above the waves.
shortDescription: A modern port city with a monumental oceanfront mosque, French colonial Art Deco streets, a small old medina, seafood and a lively café and arts scene.
metaDescription: A Casablanca travel guide: the Hassan II Mosque, Art Deco downtown, the Habous quarter, the Corniche, the Museum of Moroccan Judaism, food, how many days you need and a one-day plan.
knownFor: The Hassan II Mosque, Art Deco buildings, the Corniche, the film
goodFor: Architecture, modern Morocco, food, a stopover

image.alt: The vast plaza in front of the Hassan II Mosque in Casablanca

intro: Casablanca is a big, busy, modern city with more than three million people in the city and many more in the metropolitan area. It grew fast under French rule in the early 20th century, when planners laid out wide boulevards and built Art Deco apartment blocks, cinemas and civic buildings that still make up much of the downtown. Today it is the commercial capital of Morocco and its main port.

It is not a conventional tourist city, and many travellers only pass through the airport. But the Hassan II Mosque, completed in 1993, is a spectacular building, with a minaret of around 210 metres, a retractable roof, and a section built out over the Atlantic. It is one of the few working mosques in Morocco that non-Muslims can enter on a guided tour.

The rest of the city rewards a day or two of exploring: the Art Deco streets of the centre, the Habous quarter with its 1920s neo-Moorish architecture, the Corniche along the ocean, and a lively food scene ranging from fish grills to modern Moroccan cooking. The film Casablanca (1942) was shot in Hollywood, but its spirit is celebrated at Rick's Café, opened in 2004.

whyVisit.intro: Casablanca shows modern Morocco, and it is worth a day if you are passing through.

points.title: A monumental mosque
points.text: The Hassan II Mosque is one of the largest in the world, with astonishing craftsmanship in its carved wood, marble and tile.

points.title: Art Deco streets
points.text: The downtown is full of 1920s and 1930s buildings, which have been increasingly restored.

points.title: Habous quarter
points.text: A quiet neo-Moorish district of arcades, bookshops and pastry shops.

points.title: Modern Moroccan life
points.text: Cafés, galleries, restaurants and shops show a side of the country that the imperial cities do not.

points.title: A convenient gateway
points.text: Casablanca's airport and rail links connect to Rabat, Marrakech and Fes.

attractionsIntro: A day covers the major sights, and an extra day allows a slower pace.

attractions.name: The Hassan II Mosque
attractions.text: The great mosque, built partly over the sea between 1986 and 1993, with a 210-metre minaret and space for about 25,000 worshippers inside and many more in the courtyard. Guided tours take non-Muslim visitors inside.
attractions.tip: Book a tour in advance and check the visiting times.

attractions.name: The Corniche
attractions.text: The seaside promenade of Ain Diab, with cafés, beach clubs and restaurants facing the ocean.
attractions.tip: A pleasant place for a sunset.

attractions.name: The Habous quarter
attractions.text: A 1920s neo-Moorish quarter built by the French, with arches, souks, a royal palace and the Mahakma du Pacha.
attractions.tip: Buy pastries and dates in the shops.

attractions.name: The Art Deco downtown
attractions.text: Buildings around Place Mohammed V, the Marché Central and the boulevards, including the former Sacré-Cœur cathedral, now a cultural venue.
attractions.tip: Walk with a map of Art Deco buildings.

attractions.name: The Museum of Moroccan Judaism
attractions.text: A museum in the Oasis district about the history of Jews in Morocco, one of the few of its kind in the Arab world.

attractions.name: The old medina
attractions.text: A small, lively walled quarter next to the port, less polished than Marrakech.
attractions.tip: Go in daylight, and watch your belongings.

thingsToDoIntro: Casablanca is best taken as a series of short, varied outings.

thingsToDo.title: Tour the Hassan II Mosque
thingsToDo.text: See the prayer hall, the ablution rooms and the hammam underneath.

thingsToDo.title: Walk the Corniche
thingsToDo.text: A stroll along the ocean promenade past cafés and beach clubs.

thingsToDo.title: Have coffee in an Art Deco café
thingsToDo.text: Old cafés in the centre have been restored and are a good place to watch the city.
thingsToDo.tip: Try a café crème and a pastry.

thingsToDo.title: Eat fresh fish
thingsToDo.text: Simple seafood restaurants near the port serve the day's catch.

thingsToDo.title: Shop in the Habous
thingsToDo.text: Local crafts, books and food sold in a calm quarter.
thingsToDo.tip: A good place to buy gifts without hassle.

thingsToDo.title: Visit Rick's Café
thingsToDo.text: A restaurant modelled on the film, with a piano bar.

foodIntro: Casablanca has the best variety of food in Morocco, from street stalls to fine dining.

foods.name: Grilled fish and seafood
foods.text: Sardines, calamari, prawns and sea bass, grilled or fried near the port.
foods.whereToTry: Restaurants near the port and the Corniche.

foods.name: Pastries
foods.text: French and Moroccan pastries in bakeries.

foods.name: Café culture
foods.text: Strong coffee, fresh orange juice and pastries in cafés.

accommodation.intro: Casablanca has a good range of hotels, chiefly in the centre and along the coast.

areas.name: The centre
areas.text: Hotels near Place Mohammed V, the station and the Art Deco district.

areas.name: Near the airport
areas.text: Hotels at Nouaceur for short stays.

gettingThere.intro: Casablanca is Morocco's main air and rail hub.

options.text: Direct flights from Europe, the Middle East, Africa and North America.
options.detail: A train runs from the airport to the city.

options.text: About 1 hour from Rabat and 2 hours 40 minutes from Marrakech, with the high-speed Al Boraq from Tangier in about 2 hours 10 minutes.
CTM services run to all major cities.

gettingAround.intro: Casablanca is large, and taxis and the tram are the best ways to cover it.

options.text: Modern tram lines run across the city.

bestTime.headline: March–June and September–November
bestTime.summary: Casablanca has a mild Atlantic climate, with humid summers and cool, wet winters.

seasons.text: Warm and humid, cooler than the interior.

bestTime.avoid: Winter rain if you plan a coastal walk.

itinerary.title: One day in Casablanca
itinerary.intro: A quick tour of the main sights, easily added to a stopover.

days.title: Mosque, Art Deco and the sea
days.morning: A guided tour of the Hassan II Mosque.
days.afternoon: Art Deco downtown and the Habous quarter.

tipsIntro: A few tips help for a short visit.
tips: Book the mosque tour in advance.
Take the train from the airport, which is quicker than a taxi.
Use petits taxis with the meter.
Consider staying a night on the way to or from a flight.
Keep valuables safe in crowded areas.

faq.a: For one day, yes. The Hassan II Mosque alone is worth seeing, and the Art Deco downtown is interesting.

faq.q: Can non-Muslims enter the Hassan II Mosque?
faq.a: Yes, on guided tours at set times. Dress modestly.

faq.q: Was the film Casablanca shot here?
faq.a: No, it was filmed in Hollywood. Rick's Café is a modern restaurant inspired by the film.

faq.q: How far is Casablanca from Marrakech?
faq.a: About 240 km, by train in about 2 hours 40 minutes.
Generally yes, with the usual big-city precautions.

faq.q: How many days do you need?
faq.a: One day is enough, and two if you want a slower pace.
